claims.text: The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti high-entropy alloy is a single-phase fcc material.
Suppression of orbital magnetic moments causes the initial alloy to have coercivity below 100 Oe.
Controlled aging or compositional tuning can precipitate an ordered B2 phase within an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
FeTi or CoTi will form the proposed ordered B2 precipitates in the target alloy.
The B2 precipitates will form coherent or semi-coherent interfaces with the fcc matrix.
B2/fcc interfaces will act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Chemical ordering and lattice mismatch at precipitate interfaces generate internal strain or stress fields.
The interface-associated stress fields increase the energy barrier for domain reversal.
The distinct electronic environment at a B2/fcc interface may locally enhance the orbital-moment contribution.
Local strain fields associated with B2 precipitates stabilize the magnetic ground state.
The resulting dual-phase Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy will have a coercive field exceeding 100 Oe.
Magnetic ordering will be maintained throughout the proposed 300–600 K operating range.
The target fcc matrix will remain stable between 300 and 600 K.
The B2 precipitates will be thermally stable at the target operating temperatures.
The B2 phase is ferromagnetic and therefore helps preserve high magnetic-ordering temperatures.
B2+BCC decomposition in AlCoFeNi-based alloys increased coercivity.
Replacing ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr in AlCoFeNi substantially reduces saturation magnetization and increases coercivity.
There is an intermediate B2 phase fraction that is sufficient for domain pinning while preserving continuity of the fcc matrix.
An excessive B2 fraction could disrupt fcc-matrix continuity or cause brittleness.
The magnetic state of the B2 phase may change between ferromagnetic, paramagnetic, and antiferromagnetic behavior depending on the Ti/Co/Fe ratio.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome invokes the ferromagnetic nature of the B2 phase as a reason magnetic ordering will be retained, whereas the uncertainty field states that the same phase may instead be paramagnetic or antiferromagnetic.
The conditions field treats B2 thermal stability over the operating range as present, while the uncertainty field says stability at the target temperatures is unknown.
